messages:
maria: Heads-up — I sketched a migration plan for internal agent keys. TL;DR: move from long-lived agent API keys to short-lived brokered leases + optional operator pins for background jobs. Thoughts?
jamal: 👍 interesting. main worry is auditability and cross-project routing. leases are better for least-privilege but we lose easy long-term trace for ops unless broker logs are rich.
ashley: agree with jamal. Also background workers that run for hours need stable creds. operator pins could be a middle ground: long-lived for ops, short-lived for ephemeral agents.
sebastian: couple tradeoffs: 1) latency — minting at call-time adds ~20-40ms if local cache miss. 2) token propagation — we need a trace-id surface so downstream services can link back to the origin key for compliance.
maria: good points. Proposal refinement: broker returns {token, origin_id, audit_nonce}, and we require services to log origin_id. we keep broker audit logs immutable for 90d.
nina: implementation note: SDK changes needed — add mint() + refresh() helpers and transparent caching. Can we keep old API shape to avoid breaking clients?
maria: yes, plan is compatibility shim: if client supplies legacy agent-key header, broker can exchange to a short-lived lease server-side, but mark exchanged=true in logs.
jamal: exchange sounds convenient but increases surface for credential exfil. We should require explicit opt-in for automatic exchange and tighten rate limits.
ashley: +1 on opt-in. Also add per-project quotas and per-actor rate limits. background jobs can request a pinned lease with a higher TTL and extra attestation step.
sebastian: about RBAC mapping — we should map pinned leases to a service-actor id and keep role bindings immutable for a lease lifetime. No dynamic RBAC evaluation on every request; evaluate at mint.
maria: exactly. mint-time RBAC evaluation, then token carries role-claim set. If a role changes mid-lease, we rely on ttl expiration or active revocation. we need a revocation endpoint.
nina: revocation is doable. ops-bot can broadcast revocations to routing layers. question: should revocation be soft (deny new mint) or hard (kill existing tokens)?
jamal: for security incidents we need hard revocation. add ephemeral KV with revocation ids in the edge so token checks consult it (fast path).
ashley: that adds complexity to edges. alternative: shorter default TTLs (max 15m) for most leases and allow >1h only for pinned operator leases. Tradeoff is more mint traffic.
sebastian: we can optimize with a local revocation bloom filter updated via push — cheap checks and near-real-time.
maria: rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement broker + mint API behind feature flag 2) SDK opt-in 3) canary a subset of services with short TTLs 4) enable automatic exchange for internal infra after audit sign-off 5) pinning workflow for ops teams 6) deprecate legacy keys after 6 months.
jamal: add a step for a small perf benchmark (p50/p95 token mint impact) and an incident playbook for failed broker.
nina: I'll own the SDK tasks. assign to me?
maria: assigning to @nina. Also @sebastian can you take the perf bench and revocation design?
sebastian: on it.
ops-bot: Reminder — security review required before opt-in. Please file a formal RFC link: https://rfc.internal/agent-lease-migration
deploy-bot: Can we add a deploy window in the RFC? rolling deploy preferred, small ring first.
maria: noted. Next step: I'll draft the RFC with the decisions above and include a small checklist for canary metrics. Expect draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
